example_teams.team_notes: Have Chisa on Moonlit Clouds for the strongest possible buffing.
Ideally only run Mornye with Lynae on the team, as an alternative to Suisui/Chisa.

cons: Self-buffs CRIT stats by so much that Shorekeeper is rendered practically useless, she is hence more limited in premium 3rd slot options than most (Chisa/Suisui, and Mornye specifically with Lynae, are your only upgrade paths from Verina);
Her performance in Whimpering Wastes is vastly inferior to that of her peers, making her largely a ToA/Matrix-focused DPS instead of an all-rounder, even when optimized through Quickswap.
pros: Top-tier damage ceiling with a focus on mid-air combat and animations that are generally hard to interrupt;
Energy Regen requirements are super easy to meet thanks to her set effects and teams with high base Energy generation;
Has a ton of accessible team compositions, F2P and Premium alike. F2P-friendly while also being improvable for cheap;
Looks like Selena: Pianissimo from Punishing: Gray Raven (we like Selena: Pianissimo from Punishing: Gray Raven).

recommended_endgame_stats_target: Energy Regen: 107%-119%Lower end estimated with Rebecca+Chisa, higher end estimated with Chisa+Verina. In any case, should be very easy to meet due to her 2P Echo set giving 10% ER already.

sections.heading: Summary
paragraphs: Yangyang: Xuanling (who we will just shorten to YY:XL throughout this review) is a 5-star Havoc Sword Main DPS character who relies on Havoc Bane and Heavy Attack damage to execute pretty fast & most importantly really strong rotations that will, with enough investment, decimate her enemies, as you'll see she is one of the top DPS characters in the game.

sections.heading: Key Mechanics & Rotation
paragraphs: YY:XL applies Havoc Bane constantly with most of the attacks in her rotation, upkeeping max stacks on all enemies at all times (even in multi-wave content) is something she can handle easily. Havoc Bane constantly applies DEF Shred to affected enemies, as well as Havoc DMG Amplification to Yangyang via one of her passives (up to 6 stacks).

Her rotation relies on switching between Azure and Feather stance. By default, she starts her rotations in Azure stance. She can switch freely between both forms via her Skill, however she can do so using enhanced skills if her Melody Forte gauge is depleted fully (via Perfect Dodges or Basic Attacks). This restores her other Forte resource, Azure Plume, which enhances her Mid-Air Attack and  Azure Heavy Attack. In short, her rotation has her consuming her melody bar once, switching between both of her forms and casting her key attacks consecutively until she switches out.

YY:XL additionally self-buffs her CRIT DMG throughout her rotation, as executing it will enhance the CRIT DMG of her key attacks by massive amounts (she reaches above 500% total CRIT DMG with a standard build and team, which leads to as bonkers of a damage ceiling as you'd expect).
Finally, her Outro buffs the Havoc DMG of other Havoc Bane appliers than herself in the team on top of dealing a small amount of damage (right now, only Chisa can use this).

YY:XL's kit is very wordy but boils down to the self-buffs we detailed above, as well as ensuring that Havoc Bane is constantly applied on enemies up to max stacks at all times, even in multi-wave content, so that's really all we have to say on her kit before we conclude.

sections.heading: Meta Position & Conclusion
paragraphs: In the meta, YY:XL is a pretty imposing presence, to say the least. The nature of her kit makes her excel in single-target situations - against any boss, you name it, she does it. In spite of her Signature weapon granting her a good increase over Emerald of Genesis, she still winds up one of the most F2P-friendly characters in the game, thanks to one of her best supports, Rebecca, being free, as well as her base damage simply being super high.

However, YY:XL faces very noticeable issues in multi-wave and AoE content. A lot of her key attacks lack the AoE they would need to deal damage to all enemies in her biggest attacks' range, and a lot of her rotation happening mid-air means she is prone to missing key hits of damage that would be a great help to her multi-wave clearing. Her ability to work with proven AoE powerhouses like Phrolova does not remedy this, but she has access to generally applicable Supports like Lynae, Rebecca or even Mortefi. This makes her a powerhouse with a major flaw. Perfection in one gamemode comes at a cost in the other.

Overall, she is one of the most meta releases, but won't help you too much in Whimpering Wastes. While she still clears the content, is F2P-friendly, and has one of the highest ceilings for scoring in bossing content, her AoE abilities inevitably fall behind, particularly in multi-wave where she is prone to overkilling enemies or lacking the AoE to deal with everybody at once.

In conclusion, YY:XL is one of the best DPS characters in Wuthering Waves overall. While she lacks the tools to deal with multi-wave content as well as her peers, it is beyond the shadow of a doubt that she is one of the most meta DPS for bossing content currently, being the best by a long shot when fully optimized too. No matter how you put it, as one of the most meta releases to date, YY:XL basically cannot disappoint on practically any Wuthering Waves account. As long as you're wary of her shortcomings and can work around them, she will be an excellent pickup for your account.

synergies.commentary: Yangyang's best partners are Chisa for general Negative Status buffing, the ability to apply Havoc Bane, and increase its max stacks, providing a ton of buffs; and Suisui who has some of the best buffs for Havoc Bane consumers like Yangyang: Xuanling in the game as well. Chisa is great either as a 2nd slot with both Suisui and Yangyang, making for the best possible team Yangyang has, or as a 3rd slot with Heavy Attack Outro buffers for example. Meanwhile, Suisui always acts as the strongest 3rd slot available to Yangyang by sheer buffing amount.

Heavy Attack Outro buffers work well with Yangyang: Xuanling, and Lynae also has a rotation with strong general buffs and high personal damage which makes for a great choice as well. Overall, these picks are not far off Yangyang's best teams, as a matter of fact Phrolova is a fantastic Dual DPS pick making for Yangyang's best Whimpering Wastes teams, while Rebecca+Suisui is shockingly close to Chisa+Suisui in strength, and the other buffers make for good alternatives if other teammates aren't available.
Decent 3rd slot options if Chisa or Suisui aren't available. Verina is the generalist go-to when in a pinch for good Support picks while Mornye works great with Lynae.
